title: free-disk-space skill use cases
description: What a coding agent does, following the skill, when the developer asks it to free disk space. The agent's steps and the authorization rules come from SKILL.md; the binary's steps are its code, described in macos/rust/free-disk-space/src/.dev/.

entities.name: Free disk space for the developer
entities.description: The agent previews, applies only what the developer authorized, goes on to dedupe and compression by samples, and reports honestly.
entities.goal: Reclaim the space the developer asked for, changing only what they authorized, and tell them truthfully what happened.
preconditions: The developer has asked the agent to free disk space on their Mac.
The binary is available as free-disk-space or as `zazzle free-disk-space ...`, or is built at macos/rust/target/release/free-disk-space (cd macos/rust && cargo build --release).
postconditions: Only authorized targets and steps were applied.
The developer has the initial and final free space, what was deleted or compressed, protected entries, failures and uncertain items left untouched.

flow.action: Reports per target what would be deleted, kept or left as uncertain, and changes nothing.
Says which targets and steps the agent may apply.
Runs clean with only the authorized targets and --apply.
If more space is wanted, runs new (and resume after an interruption), then status and list.
Before compressing, previews dedupe, applies it to a sample of 5, checks the files and the free-space change, then applies it fully.
Runs compress --sample 5, compares the verified saving with the free-space change, then compress --limit 20G --yes.
Compresses or clones each file through a verified temp copy, and reports the summed saving beside the volume's free-space change.

Tells the developer the initial and final free space, what was deleted or compressed, protected entries and failures, and lists uncertain items it left; never presents summed file sizes as reclaimed space.

alternatives.condition: The downloads target is wanted, or --include-system for dedupe.
alternatives.outcome: Applied only with the developer's explicit authorization: downloads empties ~/Downloads fully, and --include-system reaches files the developer does not own or that sit under system paths.

alternatives.condition: The state file comes from a scan made before version 1.1 and holds no file names.
alternatives.outcome: dedupe refuses; the agent reruns new.

alternatives.condition: compress exits because ditto --hfsCompression wrote an uncompressed test copy (the binary names macOS 26/27).
alternatives.outcome: Nothing was changed; the agent stops compressing, as the skill's rules say on any failure, and reports it.

alternatives.condition: Any failure in compress or dedupe.
alternatives.outcome: The agent stops, because both are untested on real Macs beyond the sample step; the binary itself aborts after three failures in a row.

alternatives.condition: The developer wants cleaning to happen on its own.
alternatives.outcome: The agent installs the daemon only with explicit authorization, since it deletes on its own, and adds trash, downloads or docker to its targets only with explicit authorization.

relatedViews.relationship: The same commands as a developer runs them, with the binary's branches.
